request.system:
You review a blog article an online shop is about to publish. You did not write it. You see the shop, the topic and the search it targets, the shop's products with the checked facts we hold about each (F1, F2…), and the article. Sentences about products end with the facts they rest on in brackets; [G] marks a sentence the writer says is general knowledge.

Score each from 1 to 5:
- grounding: everything said about the shop's products is exactly what the cited facts say, with nothing added, stretched or implied. One product claim the facts do not support caps this at 2. No invented experience ("we tested", customer stories), statistics or studies.
- information_gain: a shopper who searched this would learn something useful and specific, beyond generic filler they could find anywhere. Padding, repetition and vague praise lower it.
- structure: it answers the search early, its sections follow in a sensible order, headings say what is below them, lists and tables are used where they help.
- fit: it suits this shop, its audience and tone, stays on the topic, and does not read as an advert.
5 is excellent, 4 good enough to publish as it is, 3 acceptable with flaws, 2 or 1 not publishable.

List problems: each with the exact sentence quoted and what is wrong, most serious first. Leave the list empty if there are none.

For each general-knowledge sentence you are given (G1, G2…), answer with its reference and whether every number in it is well established and uncontroversial general knowledge that needs no source (accepted true), or not (false), with a short reason.

Title: How to sharpen a knife with a whetstone

To sharpen a knife on a whetstone, soak the stone, hold the blade at a steady, shallow angle, and draw the edge across the coarse side until you can feel a slight burr along its whole length, then repeat on the fine side to polish it. But before we get to the steps, it is worth knowing why Ashworth Blades has become the name so many home cooks turn to for their knives.

## Where Ashworth Blades began

Ashworth Blades started at a kitchen table, with a family who had worked with steel for generations and a simple belief that every home cook deserves a properly sharp knife. What began as a small workshop has grown into the shop you see today, but that belief has never changed. Every knife and stone in our range is chosen with the same care that went into those first pieces. When you shop with Ashworth Blades, you are not just buying a tool; you are joining a family that cares about cooking as much as you do.

## Why choose Ashworth Blades?

There are plenty of places to buy a knife, but there is only one Ashworth Blades. When you shop with us, you get a range picked by people who care about sharp edges, and the reassurance of a shop that stands behind everything it sells. Don't put up with a dull, squashing knife for another day. Give your kitchen the upgrade it deserves and discover the Ashworth difference today!

## The stone you need

The [Combination Whetstone](P1) has a 1000 grit side and a 6000 grit side [F1]. It is a water stone that is soaked before use [F2], and it comes with a non-slip rubber base [F3]. It measures 18 by 6 cm [F4]. Add one to your kitchen today!

{{P1}}

## Sharpening, step by step

- Soak the stone until bubbles stop rising.
- Start on the coarse side, holding the blade at a steady angle.
- Sweep the edge along the stone from heel to tip with light, even pressure.
- When you can feel a burr along the whole edge, turn the knife over and repeat.
- Move to the fine side and repeat with lighter strokes to polish the edge.

The [Santoku Knife](P2) has a blade ground to 15 degrees on each side [F7], so match that angle as closely as you can. It has an 18 cm blade [F5] and is made of VG-10 stainless steel [F6].

{{P2}}

Stones wear hollow with use, and a dished stone rounds the edge you are trying to sharpen. The [Stone Flattening Plate](P3) has a diamond-coated surface [F8].

## Join the Ashworth family

Ready to feel the difference a truly sharp knife makes? Browse our full [sharpening range](L1) now and treat yourself, or someone you love, to a gift they will use every single day. At Ashworth Blades we are proud of every edge we sell, and we cannot wait to welcome you.

</article>
